Nothing else in this report needs an order today. Read the four watchlist rows as exit instructions despite the 'not yet actionable' heading above them — the red team put them there so the instruction would survive the enforce step, which strips a failing idea down to its mechanical reason. THIS IS A POSITION-MANAGEMENT REPORT AND CONTAINS NO NEW ENTRIES. The 2026-10-22 session was a violent single-day rotation and it ran straight through this book. Tech and the AI-capex complex sold off, the long end rallied hardest in two years (TLT +1.9%), commodities and independent power broke (VST -9.8%, CEG -5.7%, FCX -6.3%), and rate-sensitive consumer, staples, housing, healthcare and financials ripped (LULU +7.8%, KHC +6.8%, ITB +5.4%, DG +5.3%, UNP +3.6%). Research first read this as a growth scare and then corrected itself: gold fell 2.6% in the same session, which a growth scare normally bids, so the driver is an AI-capex repricing unwinding crowded longs rather than a flight to safety. THE DAY'S ACTUAL WORK IS FIVE EXITS. FCX, CEG, TLT, GE and SNX were all the same bet on the commodity/AI-capex/industrial complex and all five now sit with stops inside 0.6 ATR of the last close -- which is not a risk control, it is a queue. The book was concentrated on one driver without anyone having decided it should be; the rotation is what made it visible. Macro frames it: the 10-year is 5.13% against a 3.88% effective funds rate (125bp of term premium), September CPI rose 0.65% month-over-month, and unemployment is 4.2% and rising -- a stagflationary tilt. recommendations.key_risk: The driver has already turned and only the price has not caught up, which means this is being held on a technicality — one more duration-led session takes IYR through the 50-day and the short is wrong on both the macro and the tape. Being short a rate-sensitive basket into a falling-rate repricing is the kind of position that costs more than its stop implies, because it gaps. That argues for holding, and it is the case I am acting on. The case against it, which I am not dismissing: the same argument was the reason to hold the TLT short, and that one is being covered today at a loss. Two expressions of the same rate view cannot both be held on the grounds that the view is still right; this one survives only because it has stop room and TLT does not. RED TEAM ADDITION — the pairing this answers is TLT, and it is not the only one. BCC is held long on a thesis whose own words are 'US housing undersupply meeting a falling long-rate path', and this short needs long rates to keep rising. With TLT covered today the book still holds a rate-sensitive long and a rate-sensitive short side by side, and nobody decided it should: whichever way the long end goes, one of IYR and BCC is wrong. IYR is the smaller (2% vs 2%) and the one with a hard stop, so it is the side to cut first if the duration rally extends — the 99.57 trigger below is where that happens.
